relation:
relation Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every relation

  • \(\mathrm{DTsize}(f) \le 2^{\mathrm{D}(f)}\)
    BdW02
    A binary tree of depth $d$ has at most $2^d$ leaves; apply it to a minimum-depth tree.

With $\mathrm{D} \le \mathrm{DTsize}-1$ on the reverse pair this pins the two measures to "exponentially related, and no better": $\mathrm{PARITY}_n$ has $\mathrm{D} = n$ and $\mathrm{DTsize} = 2^n$, so the exponential is achieved. This is why the zoo carries the size and its logarithm as one measure and states everything else against $\log \mathrm{DTsize}$.

see also: \(\mathrm{D}(f)\), \(\mathrm{DTsize}(f)\), \(\mathrm{rank}(f)\) data/relations/13-definitional.yaml

facts: $\mathrm{Q}_{2/5}(f) = O(\sqrt{\mathrm{DTsize}(f)})$, even for relations, and even if the tree is randomized.
Size can be exponentially larger than depth ($\mathrm{DTsize} \le 2^{\mathrm{D}}$).

self.short: Minimum number of leaves of a deterministic decision tree computing f.
